function: Learned phase-shift (beamfocusing matrix) configuration of a 3600-element programmable metasurface for near-field spot beamfocusing at a desired focal point, CSI-independent, using received-power feedback (pp. 4-5, 10)
system: Programmable-metasurface (ELPM) transmit aperture, 60x60 = 3600 elements in 100 subarrays, 3-4 bit phase shifters; receive antenna at focal point; 28 GHz, 4x4x3 m room (pp. 3, 10-11)
method: Per-subarray TD3 reinforcement learning (actor, two critics) with transfer learning: policy propagation by circular-correlation similarity, quasi-liquid fine-tuning layers, and DFP policy blending (pp. 5-10)
data_channel: Custom multipath simulator with path loss and reflections (reflection coefficient 0.1) in a 4x4x3 m room, same as ref. 24; no dataset, no 3GPP model (pp. 3, 10-11)
test_conditions: Policies transferred from trained subarrays or earlier focal points, then adapted by further training; new DFPs at random 1-2 m distance, 100 Monte Carlo snapshots (pp. 10-12)
baselines: Learned: earlier DRL scheme without transfer learning (No-TL, ref. 24, same authors), and variants PP-LowECC, PP-HighECC; non-learned: exact-CSI in-phase focusing target (power density) (pp. 11-12)
metrics: Normalized power density at the focal point versus training iterations; iterations to converge and speed-up factor; beamfocusing radius (BFR) (pp. 11-13)
q1_support: p. 11: "we have considered a multipath channel model". Custom model of Eq. (1) on p. 3 (line-of-sight plus reflected paths, reflection coefficient 0.1, 28 GHz, 4 x 4 x 3 m room, same as ref. 24); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured data.
q2_support: p. 12: "for a new DFP, the policy blending scheme is run by selecting K-blending component policies"; p. 12: "reaching a training speed of about 12k which is 8.3 times faster than the No-TL scenario". Policies of earlier focal points (and of trained subarrays, p. 9) are transferred and adapted with a fraction of the iterations.
q3_support: p. 12: "Comparing the results of PP-HighECC-QLL to the No-TL scenario [24], it is also observed that the learning speed is raised about 4 times and the focused power density at the DFP is enhanced by about 20%." p. 11: "the normalized target power density, which is computed by using the exact CSI of all array elements" (non-learned reference).
q4_support: p. 2: "This modular architecture significantly reduces the complexity of the ML-based SBF algorithm" is only qualitative. The paper reports iterations to convergence (about 25k versus 100k, pp. 11-12), which is convergence speed; no complexity order, FLOPs, parameter count or runtime is given.
q5_support: p. 10: "we investigate how TL impacts the performance of SBF for different simulation scenarios". Results come from the authors' own simulation (Table I, p. 11); no link to code or data is given and no public channel dataset is used.
notes: PDF is arXiv v3 (16 Dec 2024, p. 1) of the TMC paper; the DOI is not printed in the file, but title and authors match. ris=1 needs confirmation: the ELPM is a programmable metasurface used as a transmit aperture with per-element phase shifters (p. 3), not a reflecting RIS, and the paper never calls its own system RIS; counted as a RIS of any kind. Area 3: the learned part is the phase-shift configuration (beamfocusing matrix). q2=1 rests on transfer to new subarrays and new focal points with fewer iterations (pp. 9-12), not on zero-shot testing. q3=1 is borderline: No-TL is the authors' earlier DRL scheme [24] (counted as the earlier learned baseline) but is also the method without its TL module; the non-learned reference is the exact-CSI in-phase target, an upper bound. q4=0: only iterations to convergence are reported.
